subject: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@bluewave.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@bluewave.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples

Laura — great meeting this morning. Per our conversation, attaching a concise appendix that shows: (1) how we define billable tokens for streaming responses (rounding rules and per-request accounting), and (2) the discount ladder tied to committed monthly usage.

Short summary:
- Billable model: billable_tokens = request_tokens + response_tokens. For streamed responses we round the final token count up to the nearest whole token at the end of the session; we do not charge per partial-byte frames. Example table in the attachment.
- Commit tiers: monthly committed tokens (three tier ladder) with automatic true-up at month end. Trigger for higher discount is net billed usage (after free tier and credits) exceeding the committed level for two consecutive months; alternative: a pro-rata step-up within the month on sustained usage >= 80% projected.

We prefer simple language in the contract (appendix) and concrete examples so procurement can sign off. See attached Redwood_Metering_Appendix_v2.pdf and SOW-draft.docx for context.

Next steps: 1) confirm whether BlueWave needs stricter rounding (e.g., 100-token rounding windows) or per-second rounding; 2) confirm whether they will accept a 30-day rolling true-up or require immediate overage invoices.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0136

Attachments: Redwood_Metering_Appendix_v2.pdf (15KB), SOW-draft.docx (42KB)

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@bluewave.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-22T12:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples

Marissa — thanks for the appendix and the quick summary. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement and infra: 

1) On streaming rounding: do you round per-chunk or only once at session close? If a session streams bytes in many small frames, could that create micro-charges? Our infra team is worried about bots that keep an open stream and send small prompts.
2) Commit triggers — we need clearer language around the two-month consecutive exceed condition. If we exceed in month 1 and drop in month 2, do we never get the higher discount? Is there an appeals path?

Also — we prefer the true-up to be immediate (invoice the overage at month close) rather than waiting 30 days. Can you confirm whether that changes the discount ladder?

CCing Samir from our procurement.

Best,
Laura Chen
Head of Product, BlueWave Inc.
laura.chen@bluewave.com

Subject: Fwd: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples

Team — forwarding BlueWave's clarifying questions (below). Quick asks:
- Legal: can we provide a short contract clause that explicitly states streaming rounding happens once at stream close (final token count rounded up to nearest whole token), and that idle open streams with no generated tokens are not billable? That should address their micro-charge concern.
- Sales/Prod: can we offer two options for commit trigger language: a) conservative: two consecutive months over committed level to step up discounts; b) aggressive: single-month overage immediately triggers step-up for following month (with true-up settled). Which do we recommend for a deal at $250k ARR starting?

Want to keep BlueWave at ease but also protect us from gaming. Thoughts by EOD?

Marissa

Date: 2026-11-22T15:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples

Marissa — quick thoughts from negotiation standpoint:

1) Streaming rounding: operationally simplest and easiest to justify is "round once at session close". Add explicit exceptions: (a) keep-alive/heartbeat frames that contain no new tokens are not billable; (b) if a stream spans >24 hours we cap billed tokens to the last 24h window for safety (rare, but helps with replay/gaming). That should address BlueWave's bot concern.

2) Commit trigger: recommend Option A (two consecutive months) for the public tier; for strategic customers at $250k ARR we can offer Option B as a concession but tie it to a 6-month review and include a clawback if usage drops below 60% of the trigger within 90 days. This gives BlueWave flexibility while limiting short-term gaming.

3) True-up timing: immediate month-close invoicing is fine, but we should keep a 7-day dispute window before applying discounts to the next invoice. Also propose a sample discount ladder in the appendix:
- Tier 1: 0-2M tokens/month — list price
- Tier 2: 2M-10M tokens/month — 12% discount
- Tier 3: 10M+ tokens/month — 20% discount

I'll draft a negotiation-friendly paragraph and a worked example table for legal to formalize.

- Aditya
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: hannah.schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, aditya.rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, rishi.malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Hosted pricing — discount trigger language & streaming token counting examples

Marissa / team — attached is a short, neutral clause we can propose to BlueWave. It balances clarity and anti-gaming protections. Please review and let me know if we're comfortable sending this to procurement. If approved, I'll insert the text as "Metering Appendix A" in the final SOW.

Proposed clause (extracted):
"Metering and Discount Triggering. Billable Tokens: Billable Tokens for a Request are equal to the sum of request tokens and response tokens generated by Redwood's service for that Request. For streamed responses, Provider will determine the final Response Token count at Stream Close and bill the rounded-up whole token count. Provider will not charge for protocol keep-alive frames or heartbeats that do not result in token generation. To mitigate abusive usage patterns, Provider reserves the right to cap billed tokens for a single stream to 24 hours of continuous generation and to audit suspicious streams; any disputes will be reviewed under the Dispute Resolution process in Section X.

Discount Triggers: Committed Monthly Tokens are tracked on a rolling monthly basis. A Customer that exceeds its committed monthly tokens in two (2) consecutive months will be eligible to receive the higher discount tier effective the following full billing month, subject to Provider's right to audit usage. At Provider's discretion for strategic accounts, step-up to the higher discount tier may be accelerated after a single month of exceedance under a separate written concession, subject to a subsequent usage review and potential adjustment (clawback) as set forth in Appendix B. True-up and Overages: Provider will invoice overages at month close and apply adjustments on the next invoice cycle after a seven (7) day dispute window."

If that's acceptable I'll send to BlueWave with an explicit worked example showing how a streaming session that emits partial frames is billed, and a true-up invoice timeline.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai
